title: The weather
about: How to describe the weather: cold, damp days, hot and humid climates, kinds of rain and wind, and the adjectives that go with them (heavy rain, strong wind, a mild winter).

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Weather — незлічуваний іменник: без a і без множини. Кажемо terrible weather, What lovely weather!, а не a terrible weather. «Сильний» перекладаємо по-різному: дощ і сніг — heavy, вітер — strong або high, мороз — hard. Мокрий сніг (сніг з дощем) — sleet.

items.meaning: during the day, not at night
items.example: **Daytime** temperatures in March are usually around ten degrees.
more: I can't sleep in the **daytime**, even after a night shift.
The town centre is busy in the **daytime** but quiet after six.
items.watchOut: Вдень — in the daytime або during the day, але не «at day» (за аналогією з at night).

items.pattern: a mild winter · mild weather · It's mild for…
items.meaning: warmer than usual or than you expect; pleasantly not cold
items.example: The winter here is usually **mild**, with very little snow.
more: It was so **mild** at Christmas that the kids played outside in T-shirts.
The south coast is famous for its **mild** climate.
items.watchOut: М'яка зима — a mild winter, а не a soft winter. Mild кажуть, коли тепліше, ніж зазвичай для цієї пори року.

items.pattern: in late autumn / late September · ↔ early
items.meaning: towards the end of a period of time
items.example: The apples are ready to pick in **late** September.
more: We usually go to the seaside in **late** August, when it's quieter.
There can still be frost in **late** spring, so don't plant tomatoes too early.
items.watchOut: Наприкінці осені — in late autumn або at the end of autumn (at, не in the end of). Протилежне — early: in early spring.

items.meaning: with a thin cloud of tiny water drops in the air, so you can't see far
items.example: The river looks magical on **misty** autumn mornings.
more: There's a light **mist** over the fields early in the morning.
Drive carefully, it's **misty** in the valley.
items.watchOut: Mist — легкий туман, серпанок; fog — густий туман. Прикметники — misty, foggy: a misty morning, а не a mist morning.

items.meaning: with thick fog, so you can hardly see anything
items.example: Drive slowly. It's very **foggy** on the motorway this morning.
more: The ferry was late because of thick **fog**.
On **foggy** days you can't even see the end of our street.
items.watchOut: Густий туман — thick fog або dense fog, а не strong fog.

items.pattern: damp weather · a damp flat · damp clothes
items.meaning: slightly wet, usually in an unpleasant way
items.example: The towels never dry properly in this **damp** weather.
more: Our first flat was so **damp** that our clothes went mouldy in the wardrobe.
Wipe the table with a **damp** cloth.
items.watchOut: Damp — сирий, вогкий, часто прохолодний. Humid — вологий і спекотний. Wet — по-справжньому мокрий.

items.meaning: a thin white layer of ice on things when it's very cold
items.example: The car was covered in **frost**, so I was late for work.
more: **Frost** can kill young plants, so cover them at night.
On **frosty** mornings the whole garden looks white.
items.watchOut: Іній, заморозок — frost. Сильний мороз — a hard frost або It's freezing, а не strong frost.

items.pattern: icy roads · The pavement is icy
items.meaning: covered with ice and very slippery
items.example: The roads are **icy**, so leave the car and take the bus.
more: Hold my arm. The pavement's really **icy** here.
Grandma slipped on an **icy** step and hurt her wrist.
items.watchOut: Ожеледиця — The roads are icy або It's icy: в англійській тут прикметник, а не іменник.

items.pattern: severe weather · a severe winter · severe storms
items.meaning: extremely bad or serious
items.example: **Severe** storms brought down trees all over the region.
more: The airport closed because of **severe** weather.
We're not used to such **severe** winters here.
items.watchOut: Сувора зима — a severe або harsh winter, не a strict winter. Strict — суворий про людей і правила.

items.meaning: a lot of snow falling
items.example: We had **heavy snow** in the night, and now we can't open the gate.
more: It **snowed heavily** all weekend.
Drive carefully. There's **heavy snow** on the hills.
items.watchOut: Сильний сніг — heavy snow, не strong snow; сильно сніжить — it's snowing heavily. Мокрий сніг (сніг з дощем) — sleet.

items.pattern: expect rain · expect sth to… · be expected to…
items.meaning: think that something will happen
items.example: They're **expecting** heavy snow tonight, so let's take the bus tomorrow.
more: We **expected** a grey, rainy weekend, but it was sunny the whole time.
What weather can we **expect** in Rome in April?
items.watchOut: Expect — думати, що щось станеться: We expect rain (без for). Wait for — чекати, поки щось станеться: We're waiting for the rain to stop.

items.meaning: stay warm and not get cold
items.example: Wear a hat and gloves to **keep warm**.
more: We danced around to **keep warm** at the bus stop.
A good duvet will **keep** you **warm** all winter.
items.watchOut: Keep warm — не дати собі змерзнути. Warm up — зігрітися, коли вже змерз: Have some hot tea to warm up.

items.pattern: freeze – froze – frozen · It's freezing · I'm freezing
items.meaning: turn into ice; (freezing) very cold
items.example: Turn the heating on, I'm **freezing**!
more: The lake **froze**, and half the town went skating.
It was **freezing** on the football pitch this morning.
items.watchOut: I'm freezing — мені дуже холодно (розмовне). Форми: freeze – froze – frozen, а не freezed.

items.pattern: snow / ice / the ground thaws · a thaw · thaw frozen food
items.meaning: become soft or liquid again after being frozen
items.example: The snow started to **thaw** at the end of February.
more: The river stayed frozen until the spring **thaw**.
Let the frozen bread **thaw** for an hour before you make sandwiches.
items.watchOut: Вимова /θɔː/: з th, як у saw, а не «тав». Відлига — a thaw. Розморозити їжу — thaw (або defrost).

items.pattern: ice / snow / chocolate melts · melt sth
items.meaning: change from solid to liquid because of heat
items.example: The snow on the roof **melted** in the afternoon sun.
more: **Melt** the butter in a small pan.
The ice in my drink **melted** in minutes.
items.watchOut: Melt — тверде стає рідким від тепла (лід, морозиво, масло). Thaw — замерзле відтає (земля, заморожене м'ясо).

items.meaning: very hot, like countries near the Equator
items.example: Thailand has a **tropical** climate, so it's hot all year round.
more: A **tropical** storm hit the island while we were on holiday.
The hotel garden was full of **tropical** flowers.

items.meaning: so hot and airless that it's hard to breathe
items.example: The heat in the city was **stifling**, so we escaped to the mountains.
more: The tiny attic bedroom was **stifling** in summer.
There wasn't a breath of wind, and the air was **stifling**.
items.watchOut: Задуха — It's stifling. Stuffy — коли в кімнаті просто мало свіжого повітря; stifling — ще й нестерпно жарко.

items.meaning: warm and a little damp in an unpleasant way
items.example: I always sleep badly on **muggy** summer nights.
more: It's so **muggy** today. I think there'll be a thunderstorm later.
The air felt **muggy** and heavy before the rain.

items.meaning: hot with a lot of water in the air, so you sweat a lot
items.example: The air in the greenhouse was hot and **humid**.
more: The **humidity** in the jungle was close to 100 per cent.
It's not the heat I mind, it's the **humidity**.
items.watchOut: Вологе повітря в спеку — humid, а не wet. Вимова /ˈhjuːmɪd/: на початку «хью».

items.pattern: boiling hot · It's boiling · I'm boiling
items.meaning: extremely hot
items.example: It's **boiling** hot today. Let's go to the beach.
more: I'm **boiling**. I shouldn't have worn this jumper.
The car was **boiling** after a day in the sun.
items.watchOut: It's boiling — розмовне перебільшення, як у нас «не спека, а пекло». I'm boiling — мені дуже жарко, а I'm freezing — дуже холодно.

items.meaning: a period of unusually hot weather
items.example: During the **heatwave**, the shops sold out of fans.
more: It's the third **heatwave** this summer.
Schools closed early because of the **heatwave**.
items.watchOut: Хвиля спеки — a heatwave (одним словом або heat wave), але не a hot wave.

items.meaning: a short period of rain
items.example: We waited in a bus shelter until the **shower** passed.
more: There were a few light **showers** in the morning, but the afternoon was dry.
Heavy **showers** are possible this evening.
items.watchOut: Shower — і душ, і короткий дощ. «Короткочасні дощі» в прогнозі — showers.

items.meaning: a lot of rain
items.example: We stayed in all weekend because of the **heavy rain**.
more: It's been **raining heavily** since lunchtime.
Drivers should slow down in **heavy rain**.
items.watchOut: Сильний дощ — heavy rain, не strong rain. Сильно дощить — it's raining heavily (або hard), не strongly.

items.pattern: It's pouring (down) · It's pouring with rain
items.meaning: rain very hard
items.example: It was **pouring down** when we left the cinema, and we got soaked.
more: It's **pouring** with rain, so the football's off.
Look at it! It's been **pouring** all day.
items.watchOut: Ллє як з відра — It's pouring (down) або It's pouring with rain. Підмет — it, як у It's raining.

items.pattern: a downpour · a sudden / heavy downpour
items.meaning: a short period of very heavy rain
items.example: After the **downpour**, the streets were like rivers.
more: We sheltered under a bridge until the **downpour** was over.
The match stopped for twenty minutes because of a heavy **downpour**.
items.watchOut: Злива — a downpour (іменник). Pour down — дієслово: It's pouring down. Не кажи a pour down.

items.meaning: extremely heavy rain
items.example: **Torrential rain** flooded the main road into town.
more: Our flight was delayed by **torrential rain**.
The **torrential rain** went on for three days.
items.watchOut: Наголос на другий склад: to-REN-tial. Це найсильніший дощ на шкалі: shower → heavy rain → pour down → torrential rain.

items.pattern: a flood · floods · sth floods · be / get flooded
items.meaning: a lot of water covering land that is usually dry
items.example: The village was cut off by **floods** for a week.
more: The main road **floods** every time it rains heavily.
Several fields were **flooded** after the storm.
items.watchOut: Вимова /flʌd/, як blood, а не «флуд». Дорогу затопило — the road flooded або was flooded.

items.meaning: covered with grey cloud
items.example: It's **overcast** this morning, but the sun should come out later.
more: We couldn't see the stars because the sky was **overcast**.
On **overcast** days the city looks so grey.

items.pattern: a drought · a long / severe drought
items.meaning: a long period with no rain
items.example: The **drought** lasted four months, and the lawns turned yellow.
more: This part of Spain often suffers from **drought**.
During a **drought**, every drop of water matters.
items.watchOut: Вимова /draʊt/, як out, а не «дрот». Не плутай з draught /drɑːft/ — протяг.

items.meaning: a light, pleasant wind
items.example: We had lunch on the terrace in a **gentle breeze**.
more: A cool **breeze** in the evening is perfect after a hot day.
The washing dried quickly in the **breeze**.
items.watchOut: Breeze — уже «вітерець». Не кажи a small wind; кажи a light або gentle breeze.

items.pattern: a strong / high wind · strong winds · It's windy
items.meaning: wind that blows very hard
items.example: The **strong wind** made it hard to walk across the bridge.
more: There are **high winds** on the coast today.
Ferries are cancelled because of **strong winds**.
items.watchOut: Сильний вітер — strong або high wind (тут strong правильно!). А сильний дощ і сніг — heavy, не strong.

items.pattern: a gale · gale-force winds · It's blowing a gale
items.meaning: a very strong wind
items.example: Last night's **gale** blew the roof off our shed.
more: The **gale** kept us awake all night.
Forecasters warn of **gale**-force winds along the coast.
items.watchOut: Gale — дуже сильний вітер: сильніший за strong wind, але слабший за hurricane. Storm — буря, часто з дощем і грозою.

items.meaning: an extremely strong and dangerous wind storm
items.example: The **hurricane** brought winds of over 200 kilometres an hour.
more: The island is still rebuilding after last year's **hurricane**.
Our flight to Cuba was cancelled because of a **hurricane**.
items.watchOut: Наголос на перший склад: HUR-ri-cane. Британська вимова /ˈhʌrɪkən/.

warmup.q: The match was cancelled because of ___ rain.
warmup.explain: Сильний дощ — heavy rain. Strong з дощем не поєднується.

warmup.uk: Цього року була дуже м'яка зима.
warmup.q: We've had a very ___ winter this year.
warmup.explain: М'яка зима — a mild winter. Soft — м'який на дотик, tender — ніжний (про м'ясо) або болючий.
Ожеледиця — the roads are icy: тут потрібен прикметник.
Хвиля спеки — a heatwave, одним словом.

warmup.uk: Не виходь без парасольки — ллє як з відра!
warmup.explain: Ллє як з відра — it's pouring (down). Підмет — it, як у it's raining.

warmup.q: Because of the ___, the river almost dried up.

warmup.explain: Сувора зима — severe (або harsh). Strict — суворий про людей і правила.

A.q: My jeans are still ___ from the wash. I can't wear them yet.
A.explain: Трохи вогкий одяг — damp. Humid і muggy кажуть лише про повітря та погоду.

A.q: It's very ___ for November. We had lunch in the garden.
A.explain: Тепло як для цієї пори року — mild. Soft — м'який на дотик, severe — дуже суворий.

A.q: Leave the frozen peas on the table for an hour to ___.
A.explain: Заморожені продукти відтають — thaw (або defrost). Melt — коли тверде стає рідким: лід, масло, шоколад.

B.q: My hair always goes curly when the air is hot and ___.
During the ___, people slept with all the windows wide open.
B.explain: Тривала спека — a heatwave, одним словом. Hot wave — калька.

B.q: Open the door, please. It's ___ in here, there's no air at all.
B.explain: Жарко й нема чим дихати — stifling.

C.q: We had sunshine all day, apart from one short ___ at lunchtime.
The reservoirs are almost empty after the long ___.
C.explain: Посуха — a drought /draʊt/. Draught — протяг, downpour — злива.

C.q: It's raining ___. Take the car, not the bike.
C.explain: Сильно дощить — it's raining heavily (або hard), не strongly.

D.q: It wasn't windy, just a ___ that moved the leaves a little.
D.explain: Легкий приємний вітерець — a gentle breeze. Gale і hurricane — дуже сильний вітер.

D.q: A ___ was blowing all night, and a lorry was blown over on the motorway.
D.explain: Дуже сильний вітер — a gale. Breeze — легкий вітерець.

D.q: The ___ wind blew the tiles off our roof.
D.explain: Сильний вітер — strong або high wind. А сильний дощ і сніг — heavy.

example.title: Camping in the rain
example.uk:
Ми запланували похід з наметом на кінець серпня. Прогноз обіцяв тепло й хіба що короткі дощі, тож ми не хвилювалися.

У суботу вранці стояв туман, а до обіду небо затягло хмарами. Потім полило як з відра. Ми сиділи в наметі, поки по ньому барабанив проливний дощ, а сильний вітер ледь не здув його.

До вечора поле затопило, і все, що в нас було, стало вогким. Ми пили гарячий чай, щоб не змерзнути, і сміялися з усього цього.

У неділю вийшло сонце, повіяв легкий вітерець, і вже до одинадцятої була страшенна спека. Як завжди! Наступного разу бронюємо готель.
example.en:
We planned a camping trip for [[late|a3]] August. The forecast said it would be [[mild|a2]] with the odd [[shower|c1]], so we weren't worried.

On Saturday morning it was [[misty|a4]], and by lunchtime the sky was [[overcast|c7]]. Then it started [[pouring down|c3]]. We sat in the tent while [[torrential rain|c5]] hammered on it and a [[strong wind|d2]] almost blew it away.

By the evening the field was [[flooded|c6]] and everything we had was [[damp|a6]]. We drank hot tea to [[keep warm|a12]] and laughed about it.

On Sunday the sun came out, a [[gentle breeze|d1]] was blowing, and by eleven it was [[boiling|b5]] hot. Typical! Next time we're booking a hotel.
